statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company name must be expressed in Latin script; if a non-Latin alphabet is used, a French transliteration is mandatory. The name may contain foreign words that are not misleading, must not infringe existing INPI trademarks, and must conclude with 'SARL' or 'Société à responsabilité limitée' as the legal form suffix.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Applicant may reserve the preferred name through Infogreffe for 30 days, renewable once for 30 days. On rejection, the Greffe must notify the reason; applicant may refile a new name immediately or file an emergency application (référé) with the President of the Commercial Court for an order validating registration, with an appeal to the Paris Court of Appeal within 15 days of service.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office permitted through a prefecturally approved domiciliation company for a maximum term of nine years; must maintain a real address and registered agent presence. registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Annualized probability of unannounced physical on-site inspection of approximately 20% within the first three years for VAT-registered online retailing; 5% probability prior to VAT filing; disruptive audits common in e-commerce sectors applying retail platform VAT rules.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction générale des Finances publiques (DGFiP), administered through the relevant Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE) and the official impots.gouv.fr portal. Company incorporation and statutory business identifiers are processed through the Guichet unique operated by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI), which transmits registration information to the tax authorities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A French SARL obtains its SIREN and SIRET identifiers through the INPI Guichet unique incorporation filing. The DGFiP then assigns the French VAT identification number, generally consisting of the country prefix FR, a two-digit key, and the nine-digit SIREN. The company must provide its incorporation documents, registered-office details, business activity, directors or managers, beneficial-owner information, bank details where requested, and expected taxable turnover. A foreign entity without a French establishment that carries out transactions requiring French VAT registration applies to the designated non-established-business tax service, normally the Service des impôts des entreprises étrangères, using the applicable VAT-registration process and supporting evidence of business activity. VAT registration is generally required from the first taxable transaction where no domestic registration threshold applies to the foreign taxable person.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A SARL is generally subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés). An eligible SARL may elect for income-tax treatment under the regime applicable to qualifying closely held companies, including the temporary five-year election available to certain newly incorporated companies meeting statutory ownership, size, age, and activity conditions. A SARL constituted solely among qualifying family members may elect for the family-company income-tax regime, subject to statutory conditions. France has no general United States-style check-the-box election and no general election that permits contractual hybrid classification for French tax purposes. Anti-hybrid mismatch rules may deny deductions, require inclusion, or restrict exemption where arrangements produce deduction/non-inclusion or double-deduction outcomes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, or TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For a French-established business eligible for the domestic VAT franchise, the ordinary franchise threshold is generally EUR 25,000 of prior-year turnover, with a current-year tolerance threshold generally of EUR 27,500 under the applicable rules. A taxable person exceeding the applicable threshold becomes liable under the statutory transition rules. The franchise does not generally protect a non-established foreign taxable person from French VAT registration where French VAT is due. Special lower thresholds apply to certain activities, and the applicable thresholds must be verified for the relevant tax year.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is implementing mandatory electronic invoicing and electronic transaction reporting. From 1 September 2026, all businesses must be capable of receiving compliant electronic invoices; issuance obligations apply from that date to large and medium-sized businesses and tax groups, and from 1 September 2027 to small and micro-enterprises, subject to legislative or administrative changes. Invoices must be transmitted through an approved private platform (plateforme agréée), with data exchanged through the French public directory. Business-to-consumer and certain cross-border transaction data must be reported electronically through the required e-reporting channel. France does not operate a universal real-time VAT clearance model for all invoices; however, structured invoice data, platform interoperability, authenticity, integrity, archiving, and required transaction reporting will be mandatory. Standard paper or PDF invoices alone will not satisfy the applicable mandatory e-invoicing requirements once the relevant phase applies.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods physically exported from France to a destination outside the European Union may be invoiced without French VAT if the exporter is able to prove export and the goods leave the EU customs territory under the applicable customs procedure. Evidence normally includes an accepted export declaration, a customs exit result or equivalent electronic exit evidence, transport documentation, commercial invoices, and consistent accounting records. Intra-EU supplies to a VAT-identified customer may qualify for exemption subject to customer VAT-number validation, transport evidence, recapitulative reporting, and other statutory conditions. Services are not automatically zero-rated as exports: B2B services are generally taxed at the customer’s location under the place-of-supply rules, while B2C services and exceptions require transaction-specific analysis. VAT refunds require valid invoices, proof of taxable business use, and compliance with the relevant French or EU refund procedure.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Commercial invoice identifying the exporter, customer, goods, value, origin where relevant, and delivery terms
Electronic customs export declaration and Movement Reference Number (MRN)
Customs exit certification or equivalent electronic evidence that the goods exited the European Union customs territory
Transport evidence, such as bill of lading, air waybill, courier record, or carrier delivery confirmation
Packing list and product description sufficient to reconcile the shipment with the customs declaration
Accounting records linking the export invoice, customs declaration, transport evidence, and payment
Customer and destination evidence supporting the non-EU export or applicable intra-EU exemption
Inward remittance evidence where relevant to commercial substantiation; France does not impose a universal requirement for an Inward Remittance Certificate as a condition of export VAT exemption
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: France has no general statutory 180-day foreign-exchange repatriation deadline for export VAT zero-rating. The exporter must retain reliable evidence that the goods left the EU or that the relevant place-of-supply and exemption conditions were satisfied. If the exemption or zero-rating is unsupported, the DGFiP may reassess French VAT, deny or claw back VAT refunds, assess late-payment interest generally at 0.20% per month, and impose penalties including 10% for certain late or incorrect filings, 40% for deliberate breach, and up to 80% for fraudulent manoeuvres or abuse of rights, subject to statutory conditions. False customs or tax documentation may also trigger customs penalties and criminal tax-fraud exposure, including imprisonment and fines under the French Tax Code. Repeated or intentional non-compliance may result in enhanced audit activity, recovery proceedings, and restrictions on VAT-refund claims.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France) under the European System of Central Banks and the Single Supervisory Mechanism; foreign-exchange regulatory authority is the Direction Générale du Trésor (French Treasury) under the Code Monétaire et Financier; banking and payment conduct supervision is delegated to the ACPR (Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully and freely convertible. France imposes no exchange-control authorization for current-account payments (goods, services, royalties) and maintains unrestricted capital-account convertibility consistent with Article 63 TFEU and the OECD Liberalisation Codes. The only formalities are (i) fiscal withholding at source on dividends paid to non-residents (statutory 12.8% flat-tax alignment for EU/EEA individual shareholders; 30% maximum for third-country individuals; treaty and Parent-Subsidiary Directive relief available to corporate shareholders), (ii) the Banque de France balance-of-payments statistical declaration for cross-border transfers equal to or exceeding EUR 15,000 (generally filed by the instructing bank), and (iii) mandatory EU/US sanctions screening. For an online tabletop-dice SARL with receivables collected via Stripe and PayPal, profit remittance and capital repatriation are low-friction operations subject to ordinary bank KYC and documentary profit evidence rather than to any prior administrative license.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. French law imposes no mandatory surrender, conversion ratio, or statutory deposit timeline for export proceeds. The SARL may retain foreign currency in an ACPR-licensed 'compte de devises', convert at market rates at any moment, or receive euro payout streams from Stripe/PayPal without repatriation windows. No product-specific export license is required for ISIC 3240 polyhedral dice; the sole obligations are standard customs declarations (import/export declarations, intrastat thresholds) and the EUR 15,000 Banque de France cross-border flow declaration where applicable.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Compte courant professionnel (operational account) plus compteur bloqué 'dépôt des fonds de capital' released upon immatriculation
Operational euro and foreign-currency account with dedicated 'compte séquestre' for share-capital deposit
Capital escrow account and operational current account at the local Caisse Régionale or LCL branch
Operational account and temporary blocked capital-deposit account
Operational pro account and capital deposit account
Operational professional account only; capital escrow generally referred to Caisse des Dépôts or another bank

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium as a supplementary settlement rail, but legally unsuitable as the sole treasury account for a French SARL. Constraint analysis: a French corporate registration, the bank attestation for the share-capital deposit, and the durable 'référence bancaire' expected by the commercial registry require an account with a French-based credit institution or an ACPR-registered payment/e-money institution. Offshore non-EU EMIs (e.g., Post-Brexit UK-licensed entities) cannot provide payment services in France without a separate French licence or an EU-registered affiliate; consequently, Wise (EU entity with Belgian licence), Payoneer (EU/Malta branch), Qonto (French licensed EMI), Revolut Business (Lithuanian bank), and Shine (Arkéa) are all viable for collecting Stripe/PayPal payouts, provided they hold an e-money or banking licence passported into France via the ACPR registers, are SEPA-compliant with valid IBANs, and impose the same AML/CTF controls under Articles L. 561 et seq. of the Code Monétaire et Financier. The principal legal pitfalls are the fragmentation of the reconciliation trail, the need to re-route balances to the principal French bank account, and the creation of an audit gap if the EMI does not provide line-item settlement reference data.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No nationwide statutory mandate requires a physical interview; the ACPR framework permits remote client onboarding, but Tier-1 French commercial banks in practice require the legal representative(s) to appear in person (or via their ACPR-approved video-identification tool) for the corporate account signature and AML assessment. Non-French resident directors of the SARL should assume a physical visit to the branch is required for BNP Paribas, Société Générale, and BPCE; alternatively, a notarized and apostilled power of attorney in favour of a local representative or the mobile-manager route may be accepted, subject to bank discretion. Remote opening is realistically available only through regulated digital finance providers (Qonto, Shine, Blank, N26/Revolut's French passport). Recommended dual-track strategy: open an EMI account for fast collection of Kickstarter/Stripe funds, and concurrently execute a physical-appointment Tier-1 account opening to obtain the capital attestation and establish a long-term banking reference.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unverifiable crowdfunding inflows: Kickstarter/Stripe/PayPal settlement credits arrive without structured remittance information and trigger 'high-velocity third-party collections' scrutiny, creating an apparent mismatch with the newly constituted SARL's short history.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) Kickstarter campaign verification page with project name, funding goal, final pledge amount, and dates; (ii) Stripe/PayPal merchant settlement reports and payout CSV files mapped one-for-one to incoming bank credits; (iii) anonymized backer ledger with country split; (iv) outstanding-order and fulfilment schedule; (v) SARL website terms of sale and refund policy; (vi) courier tracking (Colissimo/DHL/Chronopost) for fulfilled orders; (vii) the SARL's management accounts and standalone balance sheet; (viii) a concise business-model narrative describing low-risk handcrafted polyhedral dice (ISIC 3240).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholder capital injection: inbound SEPA/SWIFT funds from foreign personal accounts into the blocked capital account before registration are treated as suspected third-party payments or unvouched source of wealth.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) Notarized/translated statuts disclosing each subscriber's shares and the deposit clause; (ii) signed share-subscription list and payment notices; (iii) bank certificate of capital deposit (attestation de dépôt des fonds); (iv) passport copies and address proof of all beneficial owners; (v) 12 months of personal account statements for each subscribing shareholder evidencing the funds' origin; (vi) completed bank 'source des fonds' questionnaire; (vii) beneficial-ownership declaration for the RCS (form IN-1213005576); (viii) transaction references of the individual SWIFT/SEPA transfers indicating 'APPORT DE CAPITAL — [company] SARL'.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Chemical-input sensitivity: procurement of epoxy resin, hardeners, pigments, and silicone moulds is filtered by transaction-monitoring systems as 'chemical-sector materials', prompting enhanced due diligence inconsistent with the 'recreational games' classification.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) EU REACH registration numbers and safety data sheets (SDS) from the resin/hardener manufacturers; (ii) pro forma and commercial invoices with HS codes (e.g., 3907.30 for epoxy resins, 3910 for silicone) and an end-use declaration confirming use in handcrafted tabletop role-play dice; (iii) TARIC classification evidence for finished dice (9504 90 80); (iv) product safety self-declarations under Directive 2001/95/EC (General Product Safety) and applicable CE documentation; (v) customs import declarations (DAS/DES) proving lawful clearance; (vi) a supplier due-diligence table with UCC/AML questionnaires for the Chinese/US sourcing counterparts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Pre-sale business model concern: banks associate Kickstarter with refund risk, chargebacks, and failed-project reputation, and may require minimum deposit guarantees or reject the account entirely.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) Kickstarter pledge terms limited to a fixed campaign without open-ended refund rights; (ii) Stripe/PayPal chargeback and reserve statements demonstrating a sustained chargeback ratio below 0.5%; (iii) written refund procedure compliant with the 14-day withdrawal right under the French Code de la Consommation; (iv) latest Stripe/PayPal payout summaries and the projected clearing balance; (v) professional civil liability insurance certificate (responsabilité civile professionnelle); (vi) a liquidity commitment letter committing the SARL to maintain minimum operating balances for at least one accounting cycle.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: (1) open a temporary 'compte de dépôt de fonds' at the chosen bank (or at Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations if the bank refuses the blocking role); (2) each shareholder remits via SEPA Credit Transfer (ISO 20022) for inflows below EUR 100,000, or via SWIFT MT103 for larger or non-EEA source currencies, with remittance information strictly formatted: 'APPORT DE CAPITAL [Company] SARL — [Shareholder name] — quote [number] — statuts dated [DD/MM/YYYY]'; (3) tag the flow with the Banque de France balance-of-payments statistical category 'Direct Investment — Equity Capital' (BPM6/DI-1), and ensure the instructing bank files the declaration if the amount equals or exceeds EUR 15,000; (4) deliver the KYC/AML source-of-funds bundle (personal bank statements, identity documents, employment or tax records) already described in the defence items; (5) upon immatriculation at the RCS, convert the blocked account into the operating account and release the attestation. No prior foreign-exchange authorization from the French Treasury is required for euro-zone SEPA transfers; the bank is prohibited from imposing exchange-control formalities on intra-euro payments (Regulation (EU) 260/2012).
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails: (i) intra-EU raw-material suppliers: SEPA Credit Transfer using ISO 20022 structured remittance with purpose code 'TRAD' or 'PURC' and the invoice reference; execution is T+1 with EBA Clearing, at negligible fees; (ii) non-EU suppliers (China/US): SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfer for trade payables, with documentary bundle comprising supplier pro-forma invoice, bill of lading or airway bill, and the customs import declaration; standard terms '30% advance / 70% against copy of B/L' suit the modest transaction sizes of a dice-casting workshop; (iii) for individual consignments above approximately EUR 50,000, Documentary Collection (D/P at sight) or an irrevocable, confirmed Commercial Letter of Credit is legally permissible and recommended to secure supplier performance, although not expected as a recurring rail; (iv) merchant settlements: Stripe and PayPal execute payouts as SEPA credit transfers with merchant-identification codes and settlement references, which automatically reconcile against the operative IBAN; maintaining a single designated payout IBAN prevents fragmented banking references and simplifies the annual statutory auditor's cash-flow review.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD OTC outright FX forwards (plain vanilla, physically settled or cash-settled under ISDA 2002/CSA or the bank's French-law master agreement) — permitted without prior regulatory authorization for hedging of USD-denominated Stripe/PayPal payout exposures; subject to EMIR reporting and to the non-financial counterparty documentation evidencing the underlying commercial exposure.

EUR/CNH and EUR/CNY Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDF) — permitted for hedging Chinese-sourced payables where onshore CNY convertibility is restricted; the French bank requires documentary evidence of the import trade (purchase orders, invoices, customs declarations).

Cross-currency swaps (XCCY) on EUR/USD and EUR/CNH — permitted for aligning USD/CNY liabilities with EUR assets, executed under the same ISDA/EMIR framework; suitable for the SARL if foreign-currency receivables and payables become recurrent.

European-style FX options (plain vanilla, premium-paid upfront) — permitted as a pre-income insurance against unfavourable rate moves on confirmed irrevocable receivables; exotic or leveraged barrier structures are generally unavailable to small non-financial counterparties under internal bank policy.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax result return (Déclaration de résultats — Liasse Fiscale; Forms 2065-SD and 2050 through 2065-SD)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) — Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE) of the registered office; mandatory electronic filing via the professional online banking portal of impots.gouv.fr (EFI)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a fiscal year ending December 31, filing is due no later than the second business day immediately following May 1, with the standard online extension to May 15 when filed with the assistance of a chartered accountant; for any other year-end, the deadline is three months from the accounting close.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge of 10% of the tax due, escalating to 40% where a formal enforcement notice remains unanswered for more than 30 days; late-payment interest accrues at 0.15% per month from the original due date; the managing director may be held personally liable for restitution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory accounts deposit (Dépôt des comptes annuels) together with the manager's management report and the statutory auditor's report, when applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de commerce (Trade Registry) of the registered office's district; transmitted exclusively through the Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises (formalités.gouv.fr)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months of the end of the accounting period, provided the accounts have been approved by the associates; for a calendar-year company, the latest deposit date is June 30 of the following year, unless an extension of up to six months is ordered by the President of the Tribunal de commerce.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court-imposed civil fine of up to €4,500 for non-filing (Article L.123-15-2, Commercial Code), plus a formal notice to file within one month and possible penalty order requested by the public prosecutor; the omission is recorded in the RCS file and impairs the company's ability to deliver legal attestations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial owner confirmation (Confirmation annuelle de la déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de commerce (Trade Registry) via the Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, in parallel with the statutory accounts deposit within six months of the accounting close; any change of beneficial owner arising from a share transfer, such as a natural person crossing the 25% capital or voting-right threshold, must be declared to the registry within 15 days of the transaction.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal penalties under Articles L.561-5-1 of the Monetary and Financial Code: up to two years' imprisonment and a €120,000 fine for natural persons, with legal entities exposed to a fine multiplied by five; false, incomplete or late confirmations can likewise be sanctioned.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual local business contribution (Cotisation Foncière des Entreprises — CFE) settlement and activity-declaration updates
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) — Service des Impôts des Entreprises of the municipality where the production facility and storage/wholesale activity are carried on
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Initial activity declaration (Form 1447-C) within 90 days of startup; thereafter, each change of premises, cessation or substantial alteration is declared within 90 days; the annual tax assessment is paid in full by December 15 of the billing year, or by the next business day if that date falls on a weekend or holiday; monthly direct debit is available.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment surcharge of 10% of the unpaid CFE plus monthly interest of 0.2% from the due date; the DGFiP may initiate compulsory recovery (saisie-attribution / immobilisation of bank accounts) and, in the absence of the activity declaration, the basis is determined ex officio at the statutory minimum valuation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual apprenticeship tax and continuing-education contribution declaration (Taxe d'apprentissage et contribution à la formation professionnelle continue)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: URSSAF (through the annual social declarations of wages — DSN, with the special payroll declaration of the April pay)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The prior-year wage bill is reported in the Annual Social Declaration (Déclaration Sociale Nominative) by January 31; the apprenticeship tax and skills investment contribution are paid with the April payroll declaration, i.e. no later than April 30 of the following calendar year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment or under-declaration triggers the standard social-security late-payment penalty of 5% of the contributions, increased by 0.4% per additional month of delay beyond the first month, plus payment enforcement by URSSAF; the employer also loses the right to allocate the apprenticeship tax to approved training institutions for the year.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory appointment of a Commissaire aux comptes for an SARL that exceeds, at the closing date, at least two of the following thresholds after two consecutive financial years: total assets of €4,000,000, net turnover excluding VAT of €8,000,000, and an average of 50 full-time employees; a group-mandated audit also applies where the SARL controls a subsidiary and the group as a whole reaches the same thresholds.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Annual financial statements are governed by the Plan Comptable Général (PCG — French GAAP, Regulation ANC 2014-03 and subsequent updates) pursuant to Articles L.123-12 to L.123-23 of the French Commercial Code; IFRS is optional solely in the consolidated accounts of listed entities and groups that elect it for consolidation, and is not permitted for the standalone statutory accounts of an unlisted SARL.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: At each annual accounts deposit the manager certifies that the beneficial owner register is exact and complete; any dilution or transfer of shares that directly or indirectly causes a natural person to exceed or fall below 25% of capital or voting rights is a reportable event that must be filed in the Trade Registry within 15 days of the transaction, and the issuance of the K-bis extract may be declined by the Registry while the declaration is not up to date.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of associates and their capital/voting interests (Registre des associés et des parts sociales)
Register of decisions of the sole shareholder or minutes of the shareholders' meetings (Registre des décisions de l'associé unique / Registre des procès-verbaux d'assemblées générales)
Share transfer register (Registre des mouvements de titres)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (standard rate for fiscal years starting on or after 1 January 2022; reduced rate of 15% applies to the first €42,000 of taxable profit for SMEs with turnover ≤ €10 million)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate on first €42,000 of profit; research tax credit (CIR) up to 30% of eligible R&D expenses; innovation tax credit (CII) for SMEs; territorial economic development subsidies; no specific tax holiday for tabletop dice manufacturing

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065 (and annexes 2053–2057) filed electronically via the professional portal impots.gouv.fr (EFI – Echange de Formulaires Informatisé)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For fiscal year ending 31 December, deadline is the second business day after 1 May of the following year; for other year-ends, within 3 months of the fiscal year-end (extended to 4 months for non-resident companies filing via a fiscal representative)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross sales and services revenue (excluding VAT) from the sale of polyhedral dice and related accessories
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report worldwide turnover attributable to the French permanent establishment (if any); if no PE, report only French-source revenue

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of goods sold, raw materials (epoxy resin, molds), direct labor, and production overheads
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate expenses on an arm's length basis; maintain contemporaneous documentation for intercompany purchases

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Depreciation of production equipment, molds, and intangible assets; provisions for bad debts or inventory obsolescence
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply French depreciation rules (straight-line or declining balance); no special treatment for non-residents

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable profit after adjustments (e.g., disallowed expenses, tax credits)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute based on French GAAP; non-residents must file a return even if no tax is due, to claim treaty benefits

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply 15% reduced rate on first €42,000 of profit, then 25% on the remainder; deduct any tax credits (CIR, CICE)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents without a PE are not subject to corporate income tax on French-source business income unless it is attributable to a PE; otherwise, only withholding taxes apply

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 5% of tax due (10% if not filed within 30 days of a formal notice, 40% for fraudulent non-filing); interest at 0.20% per month on late payments; additional 5% penalty for failure to file electronically; criminal fines up to €15,000 for deliberate non-filing

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% (standard rate for dividends paid to non-residents, unless reduced by treaty or EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim reduced withholding tax under a Double Tax Agreement (DTA), the beneficial owner must submit a certificate of residence (TRC) from the foreign tax authority to the French paying agent before the payment date. The paying agent applies the treaty rate if the TRC is provided; otherwise, the statutory rate is withheld and a refund claim can be filed with the French tax authorities (DGFiP) within the statutory limitation period (usually 3 years). For EU/EEA parent companies, the Parent-Subsidiary Directive (Directive 2011/96/EU) allows a 0% withholding tax if the parent holds at least 10% of the subsidiary's capital for at least 2 years, subject to anti-abuse rules.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 33.33% (or 30% for certain IP); treaty rates typically 0–10% (e.g., 0% under US-France treaty if beneficial owner is US resident). Interest: statutory 30% (or 33.33% for certain cases); treaty rates typically 0–10% (e.g., 0% under many treaties if paid to a bank or beneficial owner).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Full transfer pricing documentation (Master File and Local File) is mandatory for companies with annual turnover or gross assets exceeding €400 million, or with related-party transactions exceeding €1 million. For smaller entities, a simplified documentation requirement applies if the total related-party transactions exceed €100,000.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not have a specific Economic Substance Regulation (ESR) like the UAE, but the general anti-abuse rule (Article 64 of the French Tax Procedure Code) and the EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive (ATAD) require that entities have real economic substance (e.g., premises, employees, decision-making) to benefit from treaty or EU directives. A shell company without substance may be denied treaty benefits and subject to penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of income, false accounting, or concealment of sales from online platforms (e.g., Kickstarter, PayPal) without declaring to French tax authorities
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine up to €500,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years (Article 1741 of the French General Tax Code); additional civil penalties of 40% to 80% of the evaded tax, plus interest at 0.20% per month
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for unpaid corporate taxes if they have committed fraud or used the company as a shield (piercing the corporate veil). They may face travel bans, asset freezes, and imprisonment. In cases of serious mismanagement, courts can impose a ban on managing any company for up to 15 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creating an SARL with no real business activity, no employees, no physical premises, and using it solely to channel profits to a low-tax jurisdiction or to claim treaty benefits
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits, recharacterization of transactions, and imposition of 40% penalty for abuse of law (Article L64 of the Tax Procedure Code); potential criminal charges for tax fraud if intent is proven
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be jointly liable for the company's tax debts if they have acted in bad faith or committed gross negligence. They may also face a ban on holding directorial positions and criminal penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to implement customer due diligence (CDD) for high-value transactions (e.g., large bulk orders of dice) or accepting cash payments above €1,000 without reporting to Tracfin (French financial intelligence unit)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to €500,000 for individuals and €1 million for companies (Monetary and Financial Code); criminal penalties for money laundering up to 5 years imprisonment and €375,000 fine
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be held criminally liable if they knowingly participate in or fail to prevent money laundering. They may face imprisonment, fines, and a ban on managing commercial enterprises.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting intercompany prices for raw materials (e.g., epoxy resin) or royalties for IP (e.g., dice designs) that deviate from arm's length, without proper documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment of taxable income, 40% penalty for lack of documentation (or 80% if fraudulent), and interest; potential criminal charges for tax evasion if deliberate
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for the company's tax adjustments if they have signed the tax return or approved the transfer pricing policy. They may also face criminal prosecution for tax evasion.
